title: The Canterville Ghost
author: Oscar Wilde
summary: Uma família americana muito prática compra um antigo castelo na Inglaterra, mesmo sabendo que ele é assombrado por um fantasma há trezentos anos. O fantasma tenta de tudo para assustar os novos moradores, mas eles não acreditam em medo nem em tradição. Uma história cheia de humor, com um toque de tristeza e de mistério.

chapters.title: A House with a Ghost
paragraphs: Mr Hiram B. Otis was an American minister, and he lived in London with his family. One day he decided to buy Canterville Chase, a very old house in the English countryside. Everybody told him that this was a bad idea. The house had a ghost.
“I don't want to trick you,” said Lord Canterville, the owner. “My family has seen the ghost many times. My great-aunt saw two skeleton hands on her shoulders, and she never got better.”

“My Lord,” said Mr Otis, “I will buy the house, the furniture and the ghost. I come from a modern country. We have everything money can buy. If there were a ghost in Europe, we would have it in a museum very quickly.”
“There are no ghosts, Lord Canterville,” he said. “The laws of nature are the same in England and in America.”

So Mr Otis bought the house. He moved there with his wife, Mrs Otis, and their four children. Washington was the oldest son. Virginia was fifteen, and she was a sweet and pretty girl with big blue eyes. Then there were the twins, two little boys who were always playing jokes. Everybody called them “the Stars and Stripes”.
When they arrived, the sky was dark and a storm was beginning. An old woman in a black dress was waiting at the door. She was Mrs Umney, the housekeeper.
They had tea in the library. Mrs Otis looked down and saw a dark red stain on the floor, near the fireplace.
“Something has fallen there,” she said.

“Yes, madam,” said Mrs Umney quietly. “That is blood. Lady Eleanore de Canterville was killed on that spot by her own husband, Sir Simon, in 1575. Sir Simon disappeared nine years later, and his body was never found. But his guilty spirit still walks in the house. The blood stain cannot be removed.”

“That is nonsense,” said Washington. “Pinkerton's Champion Stain Remover will clean it in a minute.” He took a small black stick from his pocket and rubbed the floor. In a few moments the stain was gone.
At that moment there was a terrible flash of lightning and a loud crash of thunder. Mrs Umney fainted.

chapters.title: The Ghost Begins His Work
paragraphs: The next morning the blood stain was back on the library floor. Washington cleaned it again, but the morning after, it was there again. Mr Otis locked the library door at night and took the key upstairs. It did not help. The stain always came back.
“Maybe there really is a ghost,” said Mrs Otis.
“Then we will meet him,” said her husband calmly.

That night, at about one o'clock, Mr Otis woke up. He heard a strange noise in the corridor. It sounded like metal, like heavy chains. He put on his slippers, took a small bottle, and opened the door.

In the pale moonlight there was an old man with a terrible face. His eyes were red like burning coals. His long grey hair fell over his shoulders, and his old clothes were dirty. Heavy, rusty chains hung from his wrists and ankles.

“My dear sir,” said Mr Otis politely, “I really must ask you to oil those chains. They make a lot of noise. I have brought you a bottle of Tammany Rising Sun Lubricator. It is very good. I will leave it here for you, and I can give you more if you need it.” Then he put the bottle on a table, went back to his room and closed the door.

The ghost was too angry to move. He threw the bottle on the floor and ran down the corridor with a horrible laugh. But at the top of the stairs a door opened. Two little figures in white appeared, and a large pillow flew past his head. It was the twins.
The ghost escaped through the wall. When he got to his secret little room, he sat down and tried to understand. In three hundred years nobody had ever treated him like this.

“He remembered the butler who ran away from a green hand at his window. And now these terrible Americans give me oil for my chains and throw pillows at my head!” he said. “No ghost in history has ever been treated so badly. I will have my revenge.”

chapters.title: A Very Bad Week
paragraphs: The next day the family talked about the ghost at breakfast. Mr Otis was a little annoyed that the ghost did not accept his present.
“I don't want to hurt him,” he said, “but if he doesn't use the oil, we will have to take his chains away. Nobody can sleep with that noise.”

For a week the ghost did not appear. But the blood stain on the library floor was there every morning, and it was very strange because it changed color. Sometimes it was dark red, sometimes it was bright red, and once it was bright green.
“That's funny,” said Virginia. She was the only person in the family who did not laugh about it. She looked sad when she saw the green stain.
The truth was simple. The ghost needed paint to make the stain, and he was taking it from Virginia's paint box. When the red paint was finished, he had to use other colors.

On Sunday night the family heard a loud crash in the hall. They ran downstairs and found an old suit of armor on the floor. The ghost was sitting in a chair next to it, rubbing his knees. He wanted to wear the armor, but it was too heavy for him, and he fell.
The twins took out their peashooters and shot little balls at him. Mr Otis pointed a gun at him and said, “Hands up!”
The ghost jumped up with a wild scream and passed through them like a mist. At the top of the stairs he decided to give his famous laugh. He laughed until the old roof shook.
Then a door opened, and Mrs Otis came out in a light blue dressing gown.
“I'm afraid you are not well,” she said kindly. “I have brought you a bottle of Doctor Dobell's medicine. It is very good for stomach problems.”
The ghost looked at her with fury. Then he heard the twins coming, and he disappeared.
In his room he cried with anger. He stayed in bed for several days. He only went out to repair the blood stain in the library.

chapters.title: The Ghost of the Twins
paragraphs: After some days the ghost felt better. He decided to try one more time. He chose the night of Friday the seventeenth of August for his great plan.
He spent hours choosing his costume. In the end he chose a big hat with a red feather, a long white sheet, and an old rusty knife. He was going to frighten Washington first, and then the twins.

At half past ten he heard the family go to bed. The twins laughed for a long time in their room, but at a quarter past eleven everything was quiet. Then the clock struck midnight, and the ghost came out.
He moved through the dark house like a shadow. The wind cried in the chimneys. He turned the corner of the corridor, and then he stopped.

In front of him stood a horrible figure. It had a round, bald head and a fat white face. A red light came from its eyes and its mouth, which was wide open in a terrible smile. It wore a long white sheet, and on its chest there was a paper with some strange old words.
The ghost had never seen a ghost before. He was terribly afraid. He screamed, ran back to his room, and hid under his bed.
But after a while he felt brave again. “Two ghosts are better than one,” he thought. “Maybe we can be friends and work together.” So, when the sun came up, he went back to the corner.

The figure was still there, but now it looked very different. The light in its eyes was dead, and the knife had fallen from its hand. The ghost touched it, and the head fell to the floor and rolled away. It was only a hollow vegetable called a turnip! The body was a broom and a white bed curtain. He read the paper on its chest:
“THE OTIS GHOST. The only true and original ghost. Do not accept copies!”
The twins had tricked him. The ghost shook his fist in the morning light. “I will get my revenge,” he said. But his voice was weak, and he was very, very tired.

chapters.title: A Tired Old Ghost
paragraphs: For the next five days the ghost stayed in his room. He was weak and sad. He did not even repair the blood stain.
“If the family doesn't want the stain,” he said, “then they don't deserve it.”

But he had his duties. He had to walk in the corridors on the first and the third Wednesday of every month. So he did. But now he walked very quietly. He took off his boots and walked softly on the old wooden floors. He even used the Rising Sun Lubricator on his chains. He did not like this, but it was necessary.

The twins did not stop. They put strings across the dark corridors, and he fell over them. They put butter on the stairs, and he slid all the way down. One night he decided to be the famous Headless Earl one last time. He went to the twins' room, but when he opened the door, a big jug of water fell on his head. He was wet to the skin, and he heard the twins laughing in their beds.
After that he got a bad cold. He gave up his plans to frighten the family. He only walked in the corridors in soft slippers, with a thick red scarf around his neck because of the cold air.
In September the Duke of Cheshire came to stay at the house. He was a young man, and he was in love with Virginia. But the ghost did not have the courage to visit him.

One afternoon Virginia went riding with the young Duke. Her dress got torn on a bush, so she came back to the house and ran up the back stairs to her room. On the way she passed a small room with an open door. She looked inside and saw someone there. It was the Canterville ghost.
He was sitting by the window. He was watching the yellow leaves fall from the trees. His head was on his hand, and he looked very sad and very old.
Virginia felt sorry for him. She decided to speak to him.

chapters.title: Virginia and the Ghost
paragraphs: “I am so sorry for you,” said Virginia. “But my brothers are going back to school tomorrow. Then, if you behave yourself, nobody will bother you.”
“Behave myself!” said the ghost. He was surprised that she spoke to him. “That is absurd. It is my job to rattle my chains and walk at night. It is the only reason I exist.”
“It is not a reason at all,” said Virginia. “And you know that you were very wicked. Mrs Umney told us that you killed your wife.”

“Yes, I did,” said the ghost. “But that was a family matter. My wife was very plain, and she was a terrible cook. But it doesn't matter now. Her brothers locked me in a room and gave me no food. I starved to death.”
“Starved? Oh, poor ghost! Are you hungry? I have a sandwich in my bag,” said Virginia.
“No, thank you. I never eat anything now. But you are very kind. You are much nicer than the rest of your horrible family.”
“Stop!” said Virginia angrily. “You stole my paints to make that silly blood stain. Then I couldn't paint any sunsets. And who has ever seen green blood?”
“Well, what could I do?” said the ghost sadly. “It is very difficult to find real blood these days. And your brother started it with his Champion Stain Remover.”
Virginia was quiet for a moment. Then she asked, “Why don't you sleep?”
“I have not slept for three hundred years,” said the ghost. His voice was very tired. “I am so tired. I want to sleep, but I can't.”
Virginia's beautiful blue eyes filled with tears. “Poor, poor ghost,” she said. “Have you no place where you can sleep?”

“Far away, beyond the pine woods,” he said in a low, dreamy voice, “there is a little garden. The grass is long and deep there. The stars are white, and the nightingale sings all night. There I can sleep. It is the Garden of Death.”
“Oh, the Garden of Death,” said Virginia softly.

“Yes. Death must be so beautiful. To lie in the soft brown earth, with the grass over your head, and listen to silence. To have no yesterday and no tomorrow. You can help me, Virginia. You can open the door for me. Love is stronger than death.”

chapters.title: The Prophecy
paragraphs: “Have you read the old words on the library window?” asked the ghost.

“Oh, often,” said Virginia. “It is a little poem. It says that when a golden girl makes a bad man pray, when the dry old almond tree has flowers, and when a child cries for him, then peace will come to Canterville. But I don't understand it.”

“It means,” said the ghost sadly, “that you must cry for me, because I cannot cry. You must pray for my soul, because I have no faith. Then, if you have always been sweet and good and gentle, the Angel of Death will be kind to me. You will see terrible shapes in the dark, and bad voices will speak in your ear. But they will not hurt you, because the powers of hell cannot win against the goodness of a little child.”
Virginia did not answer for a long time. The ghost thought that she was going to say no. Then she stood up. Her face was very white, and there was a strange light in her eyes.
“I am not afraid,” she said firmly. “I will ask the Angel to be kind to you.”

The ghost stood up with a soft cry of joy. He took her hand and kissed it. His fingers were as cold as ice, and his lips burned like fire, but Virginia did not stop. He led her across the dark room. On the old green curtains, little hunters with horns waved their hands. “Go back, little Virginia!” they cried. “Go back!” But the ghost held her hand more tightly, and she closed her eyes.

At the end of the room the ghost stopped. He said some words that she did not understand. Virginia opened her eyes. The wall was slowly disappearing, like a mist. A great black hole opened in front of them, and a cold wind blew around them.
“Quick, quick,” cried the ghost, “or it will be too late!”
In a moment the wall closed behind them. The room was empty.

chapters.title: Peace at Canterville
paragraphs: At tea time Virginia did not come down. The family looked everywhere, in the house, in the garden and by the lake. Mr Otis and the Duke rode to the village, but nobody had seen her. Night came, and the whole house was full of fear.

Then, just as the clock struck midnight, there was a crash and a strange cry. A door in the wall at the top of the stairs opened, and Virginia stepped out. She was very pale, and she had a little box in her hands.
Everybody ran to her. Mrs Otis held her in her arms. The Duke kissed her hand again and again.
“Where have you been?” asked Mr Otis. He was a little angry because he had been so afraid.

“Papa,” said Virginia quietly, “I have been with the ghost. He is dead, and you must come and see him. He was very wicked, but he was really sorry for everything he did. Before he died, he gave me this box of beautiful jewels.”

She took them through the secret door, down a narrow corridor, to a little room. There, chained to the wall, was a skeleton. Next to it there was an old plate and a jug, but they were empty. Virginia knelt down beside the skeleton and began to pray.
One of the twins looked out of the window. “Look!” he cried. “The old almond tree in the garden has flowers! I can see them in the moonlight!”
“God has forgiven him,” said Virginia, and her face looked beautiful.

Four days later the family had a funeral for Sir Simon de Canterville. They put his body in the little garden under the old pine trees. Virginia put a cross of white and pink almond flowers on the grave. At that moment the moon came out from behind a cloud, and in the trees a nightingale began to sing.
Some years later Virginia married the young Duke. One day they visited the grave together.
“Virginia,” said the Duke, “you never told me what happened when you were with the ghost.”
“Please don't ask me, Cecil,” she said with a smile. “I owe him a lot. He showed me what Life is, and what Death means, and why Love is stronger than both.”
The Duke kissed his wife lovingly. And at Canterville Chase, at last, there was peace.
